title: El tapeo y la caña
summary: The choreography of going for tapas: ordering, la ronda, invitar, pagar a escote and la sobremesa

blocks.title: El arte del tapeo
blocks.body: Going for tapas isn't one drink and out — it's a **social choreography**. You move bar to bar, someone shouts the order, drinks come in **rondas** (rounds), and the meal dissolves into **la sobremesa**, the long talk after eating. Master the flow and you master Spanish social life.
blocks.callout: *Ir de tapas / ir de cañas / tapear* — all mean 'let's go for tapas and beers'.

items.en: pour me a small beer, please
can you bring us some patatas bravas?

blocks.title: ¿Quién paga? — invitar, la ronda, a escote
blocks.body: Three things to get right at the bar. **invitar** = to treat / pay for someone (*te invito* = it's on me — it does **not** mean 'to invite'!). **Una ronda** = a round; you take turns (*esta ronda la pago yo*). **Pagar a escote** = split the bill evenly. And the final ritual, **la sobremesa** — nobody's leaving; you sit and talk for another hour.
blocks.callout: *Te invito* = my treat. To invite someone *somewhere* is *invitar a*: *te invito a una caña*.

blocks.prompt: Rafa dice *esta ronda la pago yo*. ¿Qué significa?
options: Él paga esta ronda de bebidas
blocks.explain: *Pagar una ronda* = to pay for this round of drinks for everyone. Splitting evenly would be *pagar a escote*.

pairs.left: Te invito — it's on me, I'm paying for you
pairs.right: Pagamos a escote — we split the bill evenly
pairs.note: *Invitar* here means 'to treat', not 'to invite'. *A escote* = everyone chips in the same amount.

blocks.title: Pide en el bar
blocks.prompt: Order like a local: get the barman's attention, ask for a drink, add a tapa, and offer to pay.
blocks.sample: Perdona, ¿nos pones una caña y unas bravas? Esta la pago yo.

blocks.scene: A round of cañas with Rafa and Lucía — the full tapeo flow

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.target: Venga, ¿qué tomáis? Empiezo yo la ronda.
lines.en: Come on, what are you having? I'll start the round.

lines.speaker: Rafa
lines.target: Ponme una caña y unas bravas, porfa.
lines.en: A small beer and some bravas, please.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Para mí una clara. ¿Pedimos jamón para compartir?
lines.en: A shandy for me. Shall we get some ham to share?

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.target: ¡Hombre, claro! Oye, ¿nos pones una ración de jamón?
lines.en: Of course! Hey, can you bring us a plate of ham?

lines.speaker: Rafa
lines.target: La próxima ronda la pago yo, ¿eh?
lines.spotlight: *la próxima ronda la pago yo* — taking your turn, the heart of the ronda.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: O pagamos a escote y ya está.
lines.en: Or we just split it and be done.

lines.speaker: Lucía
lines.target: Eso, y nos quedamos de sobremesa. No tengo prisa.
lines.en: That, and we stay for the sobremesa. I'm in no rush.

blocks.prompt: Describe tu tapeo ideal: ¿a qué bar irías, qué pedirías y con quién? Usa *ponme…, invito yo / a escote* y termina con la sobremesa. Escribe tres o cuatro frases.
